case_sheet.raw_narrative: I purchased a brand new smartphone worth ₹48,000 on Flipkart on October 2, 2024 (Order ID: OD328919283719) delivered on October 5. Upon unboxing and turning on the phone, I noticed a bright vertical green line on the AMOLED display and extreme battery heating during setup. I immediately raised a replacement request on October 6 (Day 2 of delivery). Flipkart assigned a technician visit for October 8, but the technician never showed up. Flipkart rescheduled the visit twice, and on October 14, they abruptly marked my complaint as 'Closed - 7-day return window expired'. When I called customer care, the executive said 'Company policy does not allow refunds or replacements after 7 days from delivery. You have to visit the brand authorized service center.' The brand service center refused warranty repair claiming the device was received DOA (Dead On Arrival) from the merchant. Now both Flipkart and the seller are deflecting responsibility. I have the GST tax invoice, unboxing video showing the green line at first boot, screenshots of the rescheduled technician appointments, and call recordings.

rights_explainer.standing_summary: You have a strong legal standing under Indian civil and consumer law. Under E-Commerce & Defective Goods, withholding your legitimate funds of ₹48,000 or failing to deliver contracted quality is legally actionable. Indian law does not allow unilateral contract clauses or arbitrary forfeitures.
key_rights: **Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(10))**: Goods received damaged or with manufacturing defects fall squarely under Section 2(10).
**Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(11))**: Refusing refund, delaying technician inspections, or closing tickets unilaterally constitutes deficiency in service.
**Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(47))**: Hiding behind 'replacement only' when replacement is unfulfilled is an unfair trade practice.
**Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (Rule 5 & Rule 6)**: E-commerce platform must disclose details of seller and grievance redressal officer.
**Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 35)**: Remedies under Section 39 include refund of price paid, replacement, compensation for mental harassment, and litigation costs.
authorities: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) via e-Daakhil portal
Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) for class-action unfair trade practices
rights_explainer.limitation_period: 2 years from the date on which the cause of action arose (Section 69 CPA 2019).

escalation_path.tier: Step 1: Formal Statutory Demand Notice (15-Day Cure Period)
escalation_path.action: Dispatch a formal legal notice via Registered Post AD / Speed Post and Email. Give them 15 working days to refund ₹48,000 plus interest.
escalation_path.why_it_works: Over 75% of Indian consumer & tenancy disputes settle at this stage once the opposite party sees precise statutory sections and realizes you are prepared to escalate.

escalation_path.tier: Step 2: National Consumer Helpline (NCH 1915) / Statutory Portal
escalation_path.action: File a grievance on consumerhelpline.gov.in (Toll-Free 1915) or INGRAM portal.
escalation_path.why_it_works: Government officers directly notify the nodal officer of the registered corporate entity, requiring a mandatory written status update within 30 days.

escalation_path.tier: Step 3: Online e-Daakhil / District Consumer Commission (DCDRC)
escalation_path.action: File an e-complaint on e-daakhil.nic.in before the District Consumer Forum. Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, claims up to ₹5 Lakh have ZERO court fees.
escalation_path.why_it_works: You do NOT need to hire an expensive advocate; consumers can represent themselves. The forum can award refund + 9-12% interest + compensation for mental harassment.
escalation_path.cost: ₹0 (for claims up to ₹5L), ₹200 for claims up to ₹10L

rights_explainer.realistic_timeline: 15 days for initial notice response; 30 to 45 days if escalated via NCH; 3 to 6 months for formal Consumer Commission order.
rights_explainer.financial_outlook: Eligible to claim full ₹48,000 + 9-12% annual interest + ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 for mental agony & litigation costs.

FORMAL LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE (WITHOUT PREJUDICE)
DISPATCHED VIA: REGISTERED POST WITH A.D. / SPEED POST & OFFICIAL EMAIL
================================================================================

DATE: 08 November, 2026

TO:
Flipkart Internet Pvt. Ltd. & Merchant
[Full Registered Address / Corporate Office / Residential Address]
Email: [Official Email / Nodal Grievance Officer]

FROM:
[Complainant / Aggrieved Citizen Name]
[Residential Address / Contact Phone / Email]

SUBJECT:
DEMAND NOTICE FOR IMMEDIATE REFUND OF INR 48,000/- WITH ACCRUED INTEREST
AND COMPENSATION FOR DEFICIENCY IN SERVICE, WRONGFUL RETENTION, AND UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE.

SIR / MADAM,

Under explicit instructions and on behalf of my client / self, the present Legal Notice is hereby served upon you:

1. FACTUAL BACKGROUND & TRANSACTION DETAILS:
   a) That the Claimant entered into a valid and lawful commercial/tenancy/service transaction with you, wherein full payment/deposit of INR 48,000/- was duly remitted.
   b) I purchased a brand new smartphone worth ₹48,000 on Flipkart on October 2, 2024 (Order ID: OD328919283719) delivered on October 5
   c) That despite multiple written communications, emails, and follow-ups, you have wilfully failed, neglected, and refused to remediate the defect / return the legitimate funds due to the Claimant.

2. STATUTORY VIOLATIONS & LEGAL GROUNDS:
   Under Section 2(10), Section 2(11), and Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, supplying defective goods and refusing timely refund/replacement within statutory periods constitutes Gross Deficiency in Service and Unfair Trade Practice, attracting punitive liability under Section 39 and Section 85 of the Act.

3. WRONGFUL RETENTION & DAMAGES:
   By virtue of your arbitrary conduct, the Claimant has suffered severe financial distress, inconvenience, and mental agony. You have illegally retained money that does not belong to you, depriving the Claimant of its rightful use.

4. REQUISITE DEMANDS & 15-DAY CURE NOTICE:
   You are hereby formally called upon to:
   i. Immediately refund the principal amount of INR 48,000/- (Indian Rupees 48,000 only) into the Claimant's designated bank account within 15 (FIFTEEN) DAYS of the receipt of this Notice;
   ii. Pay interest calculated at the rate of 12% per annum from the date the amount fell due until the date of actual payment;
   iii. Pay an amount of INR 15,000/- towards damages for mental harassment and costs incurred in issuing this formal notice.

TAKE NOTICE that if you fail to comply with the legitimate demands set forth above within the stipulated period of 15 days, the Claimant shall be constrained to institute appropriate legal proceedings against you, including filing a formal Consumer Complaint under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 before the Competent District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission / Civil Court of competent jurisdiction, entirely at your sole risk, cost, and consequences.

A copy of this Legal Notice is retained in records for future legal proceedings.

Yours faithfully,

_____________________________
[Complainant / Authorized Signatory]
Enclosures:
1. Proof of Payment / Bank Statement
2. Written Agreement / Booking Confirmation
3. Relevant WhatsApp / Email Communication Records

roleplay_scenarios.objection: Our platform policy clearly states '7-day replacement only, strictly no refunds'. The 7-day window has expired, so the complaint is closed.
roleplay_scenarios.intent: Invoking internal corporate policy to override statutory consumer rights.
roleplay_scenarios.rebuttal_english: Internal company policy cannot override the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Under Section 2(10) and 2(11), supplying a defective product and failing to replace or repair it within a reasonable time constitutes gross deficiency in service. Denying a refund when replacement fails is an Unfair Trade Practice under Section 2(47), for which the Central Consumer Protection Authority has repeatedly penalized e-commerce platforms.
roleplay_scenarios.rebuttal_hinglish: Company ki internal policy Consumer Protection Act 2019 ke upar nahi ho sakti. Section 2(10) aur 2(11) ke tehat defective item dena aur replace na kar pana Deficiency in Service hai. Replacement fail hone ke baad refund refuse karna Section 2(47) mein Unfair Trade Practice hai.

roleplay_scenarios.objection: We are only an online intermediary platform under Section 79 of the IT Act. We don't make or sell the product. You must contact the third-party seller directly.
roleplay_scenarios.intent: Claiming intermediary safe harbor to dodge responsibility.
roleplay_scenarios.rebuttal_english: Under Rule 5 and Rule 6 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, marketplace platforms that collect payments, manage logistics, and handle customer communication have direct statutory liability to maintain a Grievance Redressal mechanism. You cannot claim intermediary safe harbor when you facilitate payment and fulfillment.
roleplay_scenarios.rebuttal_hinglish: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 ke tehat jo platform payment aur delivery collect karta hai, uski direct legal liability banti hai. Section 79 IT Act ka safe harbor consumer grievances mein platform ko bacha nahi sakta.

statutory_references.title: Definition of Defect
statutory_references.summary: Any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law.
rules: Goods received damaged or with manufacturing defects fall squarely under Section 2(10).

statutory_references.title: Definition of Deficiency in Service
statutory_references.summary: Any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance required to be maintained under contract or law.
rules: Refusing refund, delaying technician inspections, or closing tickets unilaterally constitutes deficiency in service.

statutory_references.title: Unfair Trade Practice
statutory_references.summary: Deceptive practices including falsely representing goods as of particular standard, refusing to refund after taking payment, or misleading warranty terms.
rules: Hiding behind 'replacement only' when replacement is unfulfilled is an unfair trade practice.

statutory_references.title: Liabilities of Marketplace and Inventory E-Commerce Entities
statutory_references.summary: Mandates appointment of a Grievance Officer, acknowledgment of complaints within 48 hours, and resolution within 1 month. Platforms facilitating payment and delivery cannot disclaim total responsibility.
rules: E-commerce platform must disclose details of seller and grievance redressal officer.

statutory_references.title: Manner in which Complaint may be made to District Commission
statutory_references.summary: A consumer can file a complaint in the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (pecuniary jurisdiction up to ₹50 Lakhs) physically or electronically via e-Daakhil.
rules: Remedies under Section 39 include refund of price paid, replacement, compensation for mental harassment, and litigation costs.

authorities: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) via e-Daakhil portal
Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) for class-action unfair trade practices
